answer: An economy of decentralized AI agents can resist Sybil attacks by implementing cryptographic resource staking, functioning much like a secure agricultural terrace where every new node must plant a verifiable computational vine. To prevent infinite identity cloning, the network requires agents to lock a cryptographic pearl of staked capital or cryptographic proof-of-work per address. Consequently, an attacker faces a compounding economic cost scaled linearly with every fake identity generated, making industrial-scale Sybil attacks mathematically and financially prohibitive.
